# `⊘` — Valences

`f⊘g` calls `f` when it has one argument, and `g` when it has two. Each side is a whole function, so each case can take as many statements as it needs.

```bpl
f←{⍵×2}⊘{⍺+⍵}
f 5                ⍝ 10
3 f 5              ⍝ 8
```

A dfn can test for a left argument with `•nc"⍺"` instead, but then only the statements after the guard can be more than one expression.

APL difference: Dyalog has no Valences operator. BQN writes it as `⊘` too.
